decisions.executionNote: Raise and progressively pitch both wrists into elbow-up approaches: left toward the red nut, right toward the purple nut. Small initial increments preserve IK continuity.
Complete top-down wrist orientation while approaching red and purple nut centers at a safe hover height; no grasp assumed.
Descend vertically above the red and purple nuts with open fingers, stopping near the demonstrated link6 grasp height to inspect centering.
Correct the left nut's lateral wrist-image offset, lower slightly, and close both grippers. Retention will be checked visually on lifting.
Lift the grasped nuts clear, then transfer each within its own workspace toward its same-color screw. Keep both grippers closed and inspect retention and alignment.
Both nuts remain visible between the fingers. Lower them slowly toward the matching screw tips, holding orientation and checking seating before tightening.
Attempt the first gentle clockwise tightening stroke on both seated nuts with only a small downward feed; inspect for coaxial retention and engagement.
Open fingers to leave the nuts seated, then reset both wrists counterclockwise without lifting for another tightening stroke. Check that nuts stay upright.
Both nuts stayed on their screws after opening. Follow their small settling drop, regrasp, and apply a second clockwise stroke with modest axial feed.
Finish the clockwise stroke, release both upright nuts, and reset wrist yaw with open fingers. Maintain the screw axes and elbow-up configuration.
Regrasp the red and purple nuts and apply another clockwise stroke with a 1.6 mm downward feed. Inspect thread depth rather than relying on gripper state.
Release both nuts and reset wrist yaw for one more short tightening pass. The screw tips are now clearly centered in the nut openings; monitor that the nuts remain upright.
Regrasp and tighten both matched nuts through another 1.6-radian clockwise stroke with a small axial feed. Check the exposed screw-tip depth before releasing.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no previous motion occurred. Release the red and purple assemblies, lift clear, and reset yaw while the right arm begins approaching the blue nut.
The released red and purple pairs remain upright. Approach the blue nut with the right gripper from above, keeping the left arm clear for a later table-mediated handover.
Lower the open right gripper vertically to the blue nut's pickup height, then inspect wrist-image centering before closing.
Center the blue nut between the right fingers using its wrist-image offset, close, and make a small test lift to verify retention.
Lift the retained blue nut and transport it to the center for a table-mediated handover. Keep the left arm well separated at a staging hover.
The blue nut is still on the table, so the lift did not retain it. Return the open right gripper above its newly observed center for a better-aligned retry.
Lower the open right fingers to blue-nut grasp height, applying a small wrist-image centering correction. Inspect before closing to avoid repeating the missed pickup.
Shift the right grasp toward the nut center, close fully, and test with a 15 mm lift. Verify blue-nut motion in both views rather than inferring a grasp from the command.
The nut slipped sideways instead of being retained. Reopen, recenter using its new head-view location, and retry a slightly deeper grasp followed by a short vertical test lift.
The blue nut is now visibly between the fingers. Lift vertically and carry it to the center staging location while keeping the grasp closed; check that it follows the wrist.
The blue nut followed the right wrist to the center. Lower it to the table and release for a table-mediated handover; keep the left arm clear until the right withdraws.
Withdraw the open right hand upward and back into its workspace. Advance the left hand only to a separated staging hover, then verify the blue nut remains on the central table.
The blue nut remains upright at the center. Bring the open left gripper to a hover above it while the right hand retreats farther into its own workspace.
Descend the open left gripper above the staged blue nut, making a small head-view centering correction. Keep the right arm stationary and separated.
Correct the blue nut's lateral offset in the left wrist view, close at pickup height, then lift 25 mm to check that it follows the fingers.
The blue nut visibly follows the left fingers. Lift for clearance and carry it above the blue screw in the left workspace, keeping the right arm separated.
Lower the retained blue nut slowly onto the matching screw axis, stopping near engagement height to inspect insertion before turning.
The blue screw is laterally offset in the nut opening. Make a small lifted lateral correction, then reseat at the same height before attempting tightening.
The lateral correction centered the blue screw. Remove the small remaining offset, lower gently into engagement, and attempt a clockwise tightening stroke with the left hand.
Release the blue nut on its matching screw and reset the left wrist counterclockwise with open fingers. Inspect whether the nut remains upright and engaged.
The blue nut stayed upright on its screw after release. Regrasp slightly lower and apply a second clockwise stroke with modest downward feed, keeping the right arm clear.
Release the blue nut and reset left wrist yaw with open fingers for the next clockwise pass; inspect that the nut remains upright and threaded on the screw.
Regrasp the upright blue nut and continue clockwise tightening, following the thread downward by a few millimeters. Keep the right arm stationary and clear.
Release the blue nut and reset the wrist for another pass. Its screw tip still appears recessed, so inspect seating and grasp centering before more tightening.
The blue nut appears above and off-center from the previous grasp. Recenter and raise the open fingers to catch its sides, then test a shorter clockwise stroke rather than feeding downward further.
Continue the blue nut's clockwise stroke from the improved side grasp, then release briefly to inspect its seated depth and stability.
The blue nut remains on its screw but its tip is still recessed. Reset the open left wrist for another controlled clockwise pass, keeping the grasp height near the nut sides.
Regrasp the blue nut at its sides and apply a 1.8-radian clockwise stroke with a small downward feed. Inspect whether its screw tip advances within the opening.
Release the blue nut and reset the left wrist without axial motion. Check that the nut stays seated and does not unwind before the next tightening pass.
Continue tightening the seated blue nut with a closed side grasp and a 2.4 mm downward feed over the clockwise stroke; inspect the screw-tip depth afterward.
Release the blue nut to check its seated position and reset wrist yaw with open fingers. Preserve the current screw-axis position before another tightening stroke.
Refine the blue side-grasp center slightly and apply another clockwise pass. The nut remains seated, but its final thread depth is still visually uncertain.
Reset the left wrist with the blue nut released, then regrasp at the refined center for a longer clockwise tightening pass. Keep the right hand clear.
Apply a two-radian clockwise tightening stroke to the blue nut with a 3 mm axial feed, maintaining the centered side grasp and keeping the other arm clear.
Release and lift clear of the blue assembly to inspect its actual seated depth without finger occlusion. Begin returning the open right arm toward its origin along an elbow-up path.
All three released pairs remain upright, with their screw tips visible in the nut openings. Return the open arms toward their origins, preserving the elbow-up branch and clearance.
Complete the left arm's continuous return to origin and settle the right arm at its origin, both grippers open. The released blue assembly now shows its screw tip close to the nut face.
Settle the small remaining left-arm return error and hold both grippers open at origin, checking that all three released assemblies remain stable.
Hold both arms at their original configurations with grippers fully open. The three matched assemblies remain upright; allow them to settle without disturbing the seated nuts.
The blue nut's depth remains uncertain from the origin view. Approach it again with the open left wrist for a closer inspection, leaving the red and purple assemblies undisturbed.
Complete the left wrist's vertical approach above the blue assembly at inspection height, with fingers open and the right arm at origin.
The blue screw tip is visible but still recessed relative to the nut face. Center the open left gripper on the nut and descend for a final controlled tightening pass.
Close on the centered blue nut and tighten clockwise while following it downward by 4 mm. Keep the right arm open at origin and inspect the resulting thread depth.
Release the blue nut and reset the left wrist, with a small grasp-center correction toward the screw axis. Keep the seated assembly undisturbed and the right arm at origin.
Regrasp the blue nut at the corrected center and tighten clockwise with a 3 mm axial feed. Inspect whether the screw tip advances closer to the nut face.
Reset the left wrist with open fingers, then regrasp the blue nut at its current seated height for a final controlled tightening stroke.
Apply the final two-radian clockwise stroke with a small axial feed, then open the left gripper to inspect the blue assembly without holding it.
Lift the open left hand clear of the blue assembly and unwind wrist yaw for a continuous return. Inspect the released pair without finger contact.
The released blue assembly is upright and its tip is near the nut face. Move the open left arm back along a raised, continuous elbow-up return path; right remains at origin.
Complete the left arm's return to its original pose with both grippers open. The released blue, red, and purple pairs remain upright and visually seated.
